subject: RFP: Tiered Rate Holdback & Remedy Terms (Orion Systems)
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@orionsystems.com>

Subject: Orion RFP — commercial clarifications (Section 4: Billing triggers / remedies)

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks for the draft response — team reviewed the commercial appendix and we have a few clarifying questions before we finalize our scoring:

1) Holdback / underutilization: your RFP response references a retained percentage of committed spend to be held for breach/underutilization. Can you provide explicit release mechanics and timing (monthly, quarterly) and whether that holdback is refundable vs applied as credits?

2) Overages and surge months: if usage spikes above committed band (e.g., committed 1B tokens monthly, actual 1.5B for month X), how are overages invoiced? Per-token rate? Pro-rated tiers? Any caps?

3) True-up cadence & auditability: we need an annual true-up, with invoice substantiation and a mechanism for dispute resolution and independent audit evidence.

4) Remedies: in the event of a material breach or termination for convenience, does Redwood provide a clawback / refund schedule or only crediting against future invoices? We need language that preserves our ability to reconcile unused committed credits.

Attached: Orion-RFP-Questions.pdf (RFP extract highlighting Section 4).

Can you send concrete contract language samples (short clauses) and an illustrative pricing workbook with numeric examples? If you can share both this week, procurement will be able to present a final recommendation to executive review next week.

Appreciate it — 
Daniel Park
Director, Strategic Procurement
Orion Systems

Daniel — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below and I attached a worked pricing workbook (redwood_pricing_workbook.xlsx) plus a draft MOU with suggested clauses (MOU-Orion-Redwood-draft.docx).

Summary (high level):
- Holdback mechanics: Redwood proposes a tiered holdback that scales with committed spend. Standard offer: 5% monthly retention of committed spend held in an escrow-style credit account, released quarterly when the trailing 3-month usage >= 80% of the quarterly commit. If usage remains below threshold, retained amount rolls into a credit pool applicable to future invoices for up to 12 months.

- Overages / surge months: Overages are invoiced monthly at the applicable overage multiplier for the effective tier. Example in workbook: for Tier B (committed rate $0.0035/token) the overage multiplier is 1.45x for tokens above the committed band in that month. For burst-protected customers we can negotiate a capped-monthly overage multiplier (e.g., max 1.8x) subject to annual true-up.

- True-up cadence & auditability: Redwood supports annual true-ups with line-item usage export, HMAC-signed usage manifests, and a 45-day dispute window. We can provide usage logs for independent auditor review under NDA.

- Remedies / refunds: Primary remedy is invoice crediting against future invoices (standard). Optionally, for enterprise customers we can provide refundable holdback mechanics (direct refund to customer bank) if both parties agree and an escrow account arrangement is established. See Section 5 of attached MOU draft for sample contract language.

Requested next steps:
- I'm sharing the workbook and MOU now — Marissa, looping you and Monica for legal/finance input on the refundable-escrow flow and likely recommended % retention for a 12–24 month commit.

Attachments: redwood_pricing_workbook.xlsx (spreadsheet), MOU-Orion-Redwood-draft.docx (draft clauses)

Best,

Karthik — thanks for the package. Quick clarifications after an initial pass:

- Overages example: if our commit is 1,000,000,000 tokens/month and we hit 1,500,000,000 tokens in April, are overages billed only on the 500M excess at the overage multiplier? Are burst tokens pulled from a separate burst pool at a distinct rate? We need the exact invoice line that would appear so our FP&A can model cashflow.

- Refund vs credits: procurement prefers refundable holdback for the first year (we can consider credits as fallback). If refundable, what operational overhead / timing should we expect to reconcile and release funds?

- Cap: is there an absolute per-token cap for overage charges that we can rely on? Our execs want a maximum worst-case per-token rate for budgeting.

If you can provide a one-page numeric invoice example (line items) and the contract clause for refundable holdback, that will get us to the legal review stage.

Thanks,
Daniel

Team — drafted two numeric options for procurement to consider (I pulled figures into the workbook as well). Paste below as plain-model examples so Orion can see cashflow impact:

Option A — Escrow holdback (recommended for large commit + predictable smoothing)
- Commit band: 12-month, 12B tokens annual (1B monthly equivalent).
- Base committed rate: $0.0032 / token.
- Monthly holdback: 3% of committed invoice (held in Redwood-managed escrow credit account).
- Release mechanics: monthly holdings accumulate; quarterly release if trailing 3-month usage >= 80% of quarterly commit. Unreleased holdback is available as invoice credit for 12 months.
- Overage: billed the month-of at 1.5x base committed rate for tokens above monthly committed band (e.g., $0.0048 / token with cap at $0.0055/token). Annual true-up reconciles net credits vs overages.

Option B — No escrow (simpler ops, slightly higher committed price)
- Commit band: 12-month, 12B tokens annual.
- Base committed rate: $0.0035 / token.
- No monthly holdback; instead we offer a 4% uplift in baseline committed usage buffer to mitigate small spikes (operational credit).
- Overage: billed the month-of at 1.6x committed rate with no hard cap (not recommended for Orion). Annual true-up still applies.

Recommendation: Offer Option A to Orion — it balances budget certainty with operational guardrails. For procurement's ask about a per-token cap: propose a negotiated cap (e.g., $0.0055/token) for the first 12 months; after that, revert to agreed multipliers. Legal/finance note: refundable cash escrow increases ops overhead by ~2–3 days per quarter to reconcile and process releases; we can model that in the MOU.
